answer: Main work complete. simulation.py implements the approved model — 2D Ising, J=1, single-spin-flip Metropolis with beta = control = 2.0236 (deep quench, T/Tc = 0.218), periodic boundaries, 1 time unit = 1 MC sweep (N² attempts via two vectorized checkerboard half-updates), RNG = default_rng(1802725656) — and produced all 9 required artifacts with exact shapes/dtypes, finite values, and exact JSON key sets. Key diagnostics: energy per site −1.7084 (t=5) → −1.9572 (t=12305) vs ground state −2.0; m(t) wanders (±0.02 → +0.23, sign changes expected for a symmetric quench); L(t) at snapshots = [13.66, 37.01, 38.75, 38.84, 38.60, 37.09] (zero-crossing of C(r)=G(r)−m², used for all 170 times, no fallback needed); interface density 0.5 → 0.0107; power-law fit L=A·t^θ over the pre-arrest window gives θ = 0.637 ± 0.014, A = 3.23, r² = 0.992 (n=19, fit_range [5, 23]); collapse quality 0.912 (relative RMS spread 0.088) over x=r/L ∈ [0.20, 1.26]. Important honest finding: at this deep quench the kinetics nearly arrests after t≈60 (frozen finite-size striped state; late snapshots nearly identical, collapse partially degenerate) — this is documented in both metadata notes, not hidden. Dynamics correctness was independently validated: at the alternative reading T=control (β=0.494) the same code equilibrates to e = −1.725, matching the exact Onsager result −1.7279. matplotlib is unavailable in this runtime, so figure.png was rendered by a dependency-free numpy+stdlib-zlib PNG path built into simulation.py (matplotlib is auto-used when present); figure structure and panel contents were pixel-verified. Reruns are bit-identical (deterministic). Two implementation bugs were found and fixed during development (inverted acceptance probability; snapshot times 172/714/2965 not being a subset of measurement times, now sampled independently). All series/stack row semantics and both L and collapse-quality definitions are documented in the JSON notes as hypotheses; no reference values were imposed anywhere.
